body:
## Observed (instance: getwyrd/wyrd-pdca)

A wave batch (`flow 691 692 … --lanes 2`) kept cycling back to the interactive sign-off session for one bundle, run after run. The bundle sat at AWAITING_SIGNOFF with a valid `iterate-do` token in its `signoff-decision` file and §9 empty. The same decision was made at 12:43, re-issued at 19:48, and re-affirmed in a third session — the driver never recorded any of them.

Instance report with the full on-disk evidence: getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#211.

## Root cause

The sign-off leaf writes `signoff-decision` durably, but the driver consumes it only **in-process**, immediately after the session it launched:

- batch path: `_drive_wave` → `run_signoff_batch` → per-chunk `_apply_decision` (template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:688)
- single-issue path: `_signoff_and_apply` runs the leaf unconditionally, then applies (flow.py:213-218)

If the run dies between the leaf's write and the driver's apply, the decision is orphaned. The window is easy to hit: a ^C during the interactive session raises KeyboardInterrupt, which `_isolate` deliberately does not contain, so the whole flow dies with the decision on disk and §9 unrecorded.

On every later pass and every later run the bundle is still AWAITING_SIGNOFF, so the queue re-presents it and the driver opens a **fresh interactive session** for a bundle the human already judged — the decision on disk is never read. The loop is stable until the human notices or `max_passes` runs out.

Two aggravations:

- `_drive_wave`'s no-progress exit only fires when the pending queue is empty (flow.py:669), so a wave holding one such bundle re-runs the session every pass.
- `autoiterate.write_decision` (called from `_maybe_auto_iterate`, flow.py:271) writes the file unconditionally, so an auto-iterate pass can silently clobber an orphaned human decision with one it did not author.

Verified against the on-disk bundle: every `_apply_decision` precondition passes and `signoff.record` succeeds when replayed — the apply was simply never reached.

## Suggested fix (running as an instance delta in getwyrd/wyrd-pdca)

Treat a pre-existing decision as un-consumed input, applied loudly before any new session:

- `_drive_wave`: each pass applies any valid `signoff-decision` on an AWAITING_SIGNOFF wave bundle (apply-deferred semantics, same as the post-session path) before the auto-iterate block and before the interactive queue.
- `_signoff_and_apply`: same pre-apply; only a `"blocked"` accept (§6 NEEDS-HUMAN still open) falls through to a fresh session, since there the human genuinely must return.
- `_maybe_auto_iterate`: decline while a decision file exists, so auto-iterate never overwrites a human's unconsumed decision or spends budget behind their back.

Behaviour pinned by a `tests/test_signoff_orphan.py` in the instance (orphan applied without a session on both paths; blocked accept still gets a session; auto-iterate never clobbers) — happy to upstream the patch + tests as a PR.
title: flow: an interrupted sign-off session orphans signoff-decision — the queue re-presents the decided bundle every pass and every run
